$comment: Machine-readable data-ownership matrix — source of truth for the C1 write guard (guard.ts/client.ts, BE-mono-13) and the check-ownership CI rules (bin/check-ownership.mjs, OPS-mono-14). Generated by hand from project-docs/03-architecture-design.md §1 (the live matrix, already corrected for the 3 reader fixes and worker-undangan's `clients` removal) plus project-docs/12-cross-repo-integration-design.md §6.2 (planned 0013-0021 deltas on top of the live 0001-0012 migration lineage in migrations.lock.json). Do not hand-edit without updating both docs' pointer notes. `writers` is a map of appName -> writable columns for that table ("*" = no column restriction, any column). `readers` is a ceiling, not an obligation (doc 03 §1). Tables/columns marked planned-only in a `note` are not yet in the live 0001-0012 schema; they are included now so the matrix and its generated guard rules don't need a breaking change when 0013+ lands.

orders.note: Live since 0009_orders_activation.sql. Checkout -> Midtrans -> webhook -> provisioning, owned end-to-end by worker-landing. Planned additive column under 0015_orders_status_log.sql: client_idempotency_key (UNIQUE) — still covered by worker-landing's unrestricted '*' write.

order_status_log.note: PLANNED — not in the live 0001-0012 lineage. Lands as 0015_orders_status_log.sql per doc 12 §6.2. Append-only payment audit trail, owned by worker-landing alongside orders.

clients.note: Shared-write table (doc 03 §1). worker-landing creates the row at provisioning and re-issues the activation token; worker-user owns password/token_version/profile after activation — it must never write activation_token_hash/activation_expires_at/activation_issued_at/activation_resend_count. `activation_issued_at`/`activation_resend_count` are PLANNED (0021_activation_observability.sql); `updated_at`/`deleted_at` are PLANNED (doc 02 soft-delete/audit delta) and not yet in live 0001-0012. JUDGMENT CALL: doc 12/03 name no owner for `deleted_at` since worker-admin is a reader-only of this table in the matrix — assigned to worker-user (self-service account deletion) pending confirmation; flag for db-analyst/system-analyst if that's wrong. worker-undangan is intentionally NOT a reader here — doc 12 §5.3 resolves its `clients` disposition by removing the dead table object from its schema mirror (folded into BE-undangan-07) rather than granting a read.

invitations.note: Shared-write table (doc 03 §1): worker-landing creates at provisioning, worker-user edits/publishes, worker-admin does ops-override only. worker-landing reads for demo-slug resolution in catalog.ts's loadStore() (one of the 3 reader corrections). `package_tier`/`activated_at`/`expires_at` are PLANNED (0013_invitation_tier_duration.sql); `photo_cap_override` is PLANNED (0018_photo_cap_override.sql); `deleted_at` is PLANNED (doc 02 soft-delete delta). `event_type` is listed under its live name — the planned event_type->event_label rename (0019_event_label_rename.sql) is flagged in doc 12 §6.2 as the one genuinely risky migration with its own add->backfill->deploy->drop sequencing and is NOT assumed already landed here; update this allowlist when 0019 actually ships. JUDGMENT CALL: 'worker-landing must never write package_tier on an invitation it didn't just create' (doc 03 §1) is a temporal/row-scoped rule a static per-app column allowlist can't express — package_tier is listed as writable by worker-landing here because it must be set at creation; the creation-only constraint is a business-logic concern for BE-mono-13's guard or worker-landing's own service layer, not something ownership.json's column list can encode. JUDGMENT CALL: worker-admin's exact 'ops override only' column set is not enumerated in doc 12/03 prose beyond the phrase itself — scoped conservatively to lifecycle/tier/soft-delete fields; flag for system-analyst if broader ops fields are needed.

sections.note: Two writers but no column split needed, unlike clients/invitations/guests (doc 03 §1 only calls out those three as needing column-scoped writes): worker-landing seeds the 12 default sections at provisioning (INSERT), worker-user edits afterward (UPDATE) — sequential, not concurrent, and no security-sensitive columns exist on this table.

persons.note: Honoree records, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD.

events.note: Ceremony/reception records, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD.

photos.note: worker-admin's read access is scoped in practice to `r2_key` only, for the media-retention cron (BE-admin-13) — one of the 3 reader corrections. The matrix's reader ceiling is table-level, not column-level (doc 03 §1: 'readers are a ceiling, not an obligation'), so worker-admin is technically free to read other columns of this table; it is documented here as not needing to.

story_items.note: "Our Story" timeline items, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD.

gift_accounts.note: Destination bank/e-wallet accounts, edited only via worker-user's content CRUD.

guests.note: Shared-write table (doc 03 §1): worker-user owns CRUD + check-in; worker-undangan must write nothing except opened_at/opened_count (the open-tracking increment in loadStore()/data.ts). worker-landing reads for demo-guest-token resolution in catalog.ts's loadStore() (one of the 3 reader corrections). `checked_in_by`/`checkin_method` are PLANNED (0014_checkin_attribution.sql); `updated_at` is PLANNED (doc 02 audit-field delta).

rsvp.note: worker-undangan writes guest submissions (upsert per guest_id); worker-user moderates/deletes. No column split called out in doc 03 §1 for this group.

wishes.note: worker-undangan writes guest submissions (token optional, guest_id nullable); worker-user moderates/deletes.

gifts.note: worker-undangan writes guest submissions (token optional); worker-user moderates/deletes.

templates.note: Global template catalog, admin-curated, unrestricted read by all 3 other services.

wa_templates.note: Global WA message presets, admin-curated. Planned rename event_type->tag (0019_event_label_rename.sql, doc 12 §6.2) does not change ownership since worker-admin already has unrestricted '*' write.

testimonials.note: PLANNED — not in the live 0001-0012 lineage. Lands as 0016_testimonials.sql per doc 12 §6.2, unchanged content vs. the archived canonical design.

invitation_domains.note: PLANNED — not in the live 0001-0012 lineage. Lands as 0017_custom_domains.sql per doc 12 §6.2, folding in the `kind` (managed/byo) column from the start. worker-user requests a domain, worker-admin verifies/activates/removes it. JUDGMENT CALL: doc 12/03 describe this as a workflow-state distinction (who may move the domain through which status), not a column-level restriction, and neither doc gives this planned table's exact column list — modeled here as unrestricted '*' for both writers pending the real 0017 migration; revisit if a security-sensitive column (e.g. a verification secret) is added.

admins.note: No other service is a declared reader per doc 03 §1's matrix ('—'). worker-undangan's schema mirror must not define this table at all (R5).
